subject: SapphireCloud gateway integration — reference design & validation
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@sapphirecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Lake <devon.lake@sapphirecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood + SapphireCloud gateway: kickoff and reference design request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profiles. We're ready to validate a production reference design for our managed gateway (SapphireEdge) that will proxy requests to Redwood Dedicated instances.

Key asks to start:
- A concise reference architecture showing where the gateway sits (sidecar vs. proxy) and auth flows (mTLS, token exchange).
- Expected 95th-percentile latency targets for 512-token generations over the Dedicated config we discussed.
- A minimal smoke-test plan we can run in our staging environment.

Can you loop in the right engineering folks and share a first-pass doc? We have a target to complete validation by Apr 30 to support our Q2 launch.

Best,
Sophie Turner
Director, Integrations | SapphireCloud
[Attachment: product-brief-sapphireedge.pdf (PDF)]

----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@sapphirecloud.com>
Cc: Devon Lake <devon.lake@sapphirecloud.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood + SapphireCloud gateway: kickoff and reference design request

Thanks Sophie — looping in Sergio and Lauren for architecture and PM.

Sergio / Lauren: can you review the asks and propose who will own the reference doc and smoke tests? My plan: Sergio to author a first-pass reference design (sidecar + proxy variants) and include ops runbook for auth, routing, and fallbacks; Lauren will draft a mutual action plan and timeline.

Sophie: we can meet Wed morning to walk through the design. I put together a quick set of acceptance criteria to guide the tests:
- Functional: end-to-end tokenized request -> Redwood response via gateway, header preservation, and user attribution.
- Performance: 95th < 120ms for small generation (<=128 tokens) in our Dedicated baseline; 95th < 220ms for 512 tokens.
- Resilience: graceful fallback to a low-cost model variant when Dedicated pool is saturated.

I'll attach a skeleton ref-design by EOD.

-Karthik
VP, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@sapphirecloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood — SapphireCloud reference design draft (v1)

Hi Sophie, Karthik, Lauren —

Attached is v1 of the reference design: redwood-sapphire-refdesign-v1.pdf. Summary highlights:
- Two deployment patterns: Gateway-sidecar (preferred for per-tenant routing + KV cache co-location) and Gateway-proxy (simpler, central proxy for multi-tenant customers).
- Auth: mTLS between gateway and Redwood Dedicated control plane + ephemeral JWT exchange per request for tenant attribution.
- Batching & cache: recommend per-tenant prefix caching at gateway layer + Redwood-side KV cache for model context.
- Latency guidance: measured baseline (internal) shows 95th of 512-token gen ~190ms on Dedicated A100 equivalent; recommending target SLA 220ms to allow network delta.

Smoke test plan (short):
1) Connectivity: mTLS handshake success + token exchange.
2) Functional: 50 sequential requests, verify headers and attribution.
3) Performance: 100 concurrent small (<=128) requests and 20 concurrent 512-token requests; capture p50/p95/p99.
4) Failure modes: simulate pod eviction, verify graceful fallback and error codes.

Action items:
- Sophie/Devon: run the smoke test in staging and return the results/logs.
- Karthik: confirm if we should include a sample sidecar Helm chart.
- Lauren: I'll hand off the mutual action plan after your timeline is set.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sapphire-refdesign-v1.pdf (PDF)]

----

From: Devon Lake <devon.lake@sapphirecloud.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@sapphirecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 17:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood — SapphireCloud reference design draft (v1) — smoke results

Sergio / team —

We ran the smoke tests in our staging cluster this morning and attached a zip with logs and a short CSV of latency samples: sapphire-gw-smoke-results-20270421.zip. Quick summary:
- Connectivity & auth: PASS (mTLS + token exchange successful across 3 regions).
- Functional checks: PASS (headers preserved; user attribution correct).
- Performance: small gen p95 88ms; 512-token p95 205ms (within the 220ms guidance).
- Failure injection: when we evicted a Dedicated pod, gateway correctly rerouted to a fallback model, but we saw an increase in p99 to ~420ms for a ~30s window.

Notes / asks:
- Can you confirm any recommended tuning for the fallback path to reduce the p99 spike?
- Would appreciate the sample sidecar Helm chart if available.

Thanks — attaching logs.

Devon Lake
Staff Engineer, Platform | SapphireCloud
[Attachment: sapphire-gw-smoke-results-20270421.zip (ZIP)]

----

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@sapphirecloud.com>, Devon Lake <devon.lake@sapphirecloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood — SapphireCloud reference design draft (v1) — next steps and acceptance

Thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed logs, Devon. Great to see p95 headroom. A few follow-ups and commitments from our side:

- Sergio will iterate on the fallback path: implement an async warm-cache priming and a short token-prefetch window to reduce cold start latency on fallback. Expect a patch by Apr 27.
- We'll provide a sample sidecar Helm chart and a minimal Kubernetes manifest by Apr 24 (I'll share Drive link).
- Acceptance criteria to close validation:
  * All smoke tests PASS in staging;
  * 512-token p95 <= 220ms sustained across a 10-minute run;
  * No >30s sustained p99 spikes during a 5-minute rolling window under pod eviction tests.

Sophie / Devon: if that aligns, we'll mark this reference validation as "Accepted" once we receive a confirmatory run from you.

I'll attach the mutual action plan and link the Drive folder in a follow-up.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior PM, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-sapphire-v1.docx (DOCX)]
